Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for issue #6305: reject guarded git writes when the Git override can't be resolved

Planning ref: `c9de2b91ee58275c20371933b6028d0434172190` on `claude/sync-pr-merge-guard-twin`. That matches the integration-branch metadata, so there's no mismatch. The dependency #6304 (numeric refspec dropped before a redirection) is closed with `ai:merged`.

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion
Reuse-audit: extends _guarded_git_invocations
Scope-mode justification: The finding names `GIT_DIR+=…` / `GIT_WORK_TREE+=…`. Running the parser at the planning head shows the same defect in two more shapes: the guard checks the session checkout instead of the repository Git will actually use. (1) `GIT_DIR+=/x git commit` only gets a non-blocking warning, then is checked against the session checkout; from a default-branch checkout it is silently allowed. `push` currently gets an "ask" prompt, but a human can still approve it, and the check still runs against the wrong checkout. (2) Earlier shell-state changes such as `export GIT_DIR=/x; git push origin HEAD`, `declare -x GIT_DIR=…`, a standalone `GIT_DIR=…;` segment, or `unset GIT_DIR` are checked against the session checkout with no warning at all. Closing every instance in the same tokenizer loop costs well under 30 extra lines, adds no dependency and no new interface. The Boil the Lake rule (completeness serves Correctness & safety, which ranks above Speed in §6) therefore picks the complete fix. The scope stays inside the one hook file, its byte-identical template twin, its test module and a changelog fragment. Wrapper forms that `git_subcommands` deliberately does not track (`env GIT_DIR=… git`, `sudo git`) and the existing `cd $VAR` / `source` / `eval` uncertainty paths are not changed.

Automation / §20 surface:
- No new script, workflow or supervisor. The change only modifies an existing hook, which Claude Code already runs as a PreToolUse hook on every Bash call through `.claude/settings.json` (and `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json` for consumers). No scheduler wiring is needed.
- No DB work. No `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.
- No workflow file grows, so §24 does not apply.

1. Files likely to change
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: parser and evaluator change, plus the module docstring.
- `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: byte-identical copy of the above. `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py::test_template_copies_are_identical` enforces this, and the branch name is about keeping the twin in sync.
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`: rewrite the two tests that assert the old fallback behaviour (around lines 844–877) and add new tests.
- `changelog.d/6305-pr-merge-guard-unresolved-git-override.md` (new): a `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` fragment in the same style as `changelog.d/6322-pr-merge-guard-single-json-output.md`.

2. Functions / modules to implement
a) `_GitInvocation` (NamedTuple, around line 181): append a field `override_unresolved: bool = False` at the end. It has a default, so every existing positional construction still works.

b) `_guarded_git_invocations(command, checkout)` (lines 347–432):
- Add one local flag that carries across segments, for example `git_override_shell_state_unknown = False`. Check the name is unique in the function first.
- Before the leading-assignment loop (after the existing `pushd/popd/eval/...` check), detect shell-state Git overrides:
  - If `tokens[0]` is one of `export`, `declare`, `typeset`, `readonly`, `local` or `unset`, and any later token, after splitting on the first `=` and removing a trailing `+`, is `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE`, set the flag and `continue`.
  - Example tokens: `GIT_DIR=/x`, `GIT_DIR+=/x`, a bare `GIT_DIR`, or `-x` followed by `GIT_DIR=…`.
- In the existing assignment loop:
  - A prefix `GIT_DIR+=` / `GIT_WORK_TREE+=` marks the current command as unresolved, using a per-segment flag such as `appended_override = True`. Keep the existing `working_directory = None` line so cd tracking is unchanged.
  - When the loop consumes every token (a segment that is only assignments) and any assigned name is `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE`, in either `=` or `+=` form, set the cross-segment flag. A standalone shell assignment only reaches git if the variable is already exported, which the hook cannot know.
- When building the `_GitInvocation`: if `appended_override` or `git_override_shell_state_unknown` is true, emit `_GitInvocation(checkout, {}, subcommand, args, "could not resolve the git directory/work-tree override", override_unresolved=True)`. Otherwise keep the current construction unchanged.
- Literal prefix overrides (`GIT_DIR=/abs/.git git push`, `--git-dir=`, `--work-tree=`, `-C`) keep their current resolution. That path is correct and is already covered by the tests around lines 778–809.

c) `_evaluate_bash(payload)` (lines 1316–1445): at the top of the `for invocation in …` loop, before the push-warning handling, add:
`if invocation.override_unresolved: blocks.append(<unresolved-override message for invocation.subcommand>); continue`
- This never builds targets, never runs `git rev-parse` / `current_branch` against the session checkout, and never makes a PR API call for that invocation.
- Because `blocks` is non-empty, the function returns `2` with the message on stderr. That is the existing block path and the existing single-JSON-output contract from #6322, with no ask decision.
- The existing `_guard_disabled()` kill switch and the API-write precedence stay ahead of this check, unchanged.

d) New module-level message builder, for example `_unresolved_override_block_message(subcommand: str) -> str`. Grep first to confirm the name is unused. Message text:
"BLOCKED: merged-PR guard (CLAUDE.md §21) cannot tell which repository this `git <subcommand>` writes to: the command appends to, exports, declares, assigns or unsets GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE through shell state, which the guard does not evaluate. Re-run it with a literal override, for example `GIT_DIR=/abs/path/.git GIT_WORK_TREE=/abs/path git <subcommand> …` or `git -C /abs/path <subcommand> …`, so the guard can check that repository."
- The message must not echo the raw override value, so attacker-chosen text never reaches the prompt or the log verbatim.

e) Module docstring (lines 13–20): add one sentence saying guarded writes whose git-directory/work-tree override depends on shell state (an appended prefix, or an earlier export/declare/assignment/unset in the same command) are blocked rather than checked against the session checkout.

3. Data structures affected
- `_GitInvocation` gains `override_unresolved: bool = False`, appended last with a default.
- No persisted state, cache format (`_cache_path` / `_read_cache`), JSON output shape or env var changes.

4. API / interface changes
- Hook behaviour changes for the shapes listed below. Each now exits `2` with the `BLOCKED:` message on stderr. Before, they either warned (`commit`), asked (`push`) or passed silently (`export …;`).
  - `GIT_DIR+=… git commit|push`
  - `GIT_WORK_TREE+=… git commit|push`
  - `<prefix assignments> GIT_DIR+=… git …`
  - `export|declare|typeset|readonly|local|unset … GIT_DIR|GIT_WORK_TREE …` followed by a later `git commit|push` in the same command, with any operator in between
  - A standalone `GIT_DIR=…` / `GIT_WORK_TREE=…` segment followed by a guarded git command
- No CLI flag, env var, log key or settings change.

## Decisions
### D1 — Block deterministically instead of asking or falling back to the session checkout
- Chosen: return exit 2 with a block message for any guarded invocation whose Git override is unresolved, and never evaluate the session checkout for it.
- Alternatives considered: (a) resolve `GIT_DIR+=v` as `os.environ.get("GIT_DIR", "") + v`; (b) keep the "ask" prompt for push and add an ask for commit.
- Why: the hook's environment is not the Bash shell's environment (the profile, earlier `export`s and Claude Code's own env can all differ), so (a) can resolve to the wrong repository, which is exactly the finding. (b) keeps a human-approvable bypass and still runs the check against the wrong checkout. The recommendation explicitly allows deterministic rejection. A literal rewrite is always available, so a false block costs one re-run.

### D2 — Treat earlier shell-level changes to GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE as unresolved for every later guarded git in the command
- Chosen: a flag that stays set across segments, set by `export/declare/typeset/readonly/local/unset` naming those variables or by a standalone assignment segment.
- Alternatives considered: fix only the `+=` prefix form named in the finding; or try to model the export semantics.
- Why: the probe showed `export GIT_DIR=/x; git push` currently runs the check against the session checkout with no warning at all, which is the same class of defect. Modelling shell semantics across `;`, `&&` and `||` is error-prone, and the conservative sticky flag fails closed.

### D3 — Leave the `cd $VAR` / `source` / `eval` uncertainty paths and `env`/`sudo` wrappers unchanged
- Chosen: out of scope.
- Alternatives considered: block every uncertain directory as well.
- Why: those paths don't involve a Git override, they have existing tests that assert "ask" (for example around line 836), `git_subcommands` deliberately accepts missing wrapper-prefixed forms, and blocking common `source .venv/bin/activate && git commit` flows would be a broad behaviour change without approval. This is recorded as a residual risk below.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the Bash command text comes from the model and is untrusted. The guard is a PreToolUse enforcement point for CLAUDE.md §21, so it must fail closed when it cannot identify the repository being written.
